big: Every time a vehicle crosses a toll plaza, money flows to someone. An InvIT lets investors own a share of such assets: toll roads, power lines and pipelines, held through a listed trust.

lines: How is it different from a REIT?

It works like a REIT, but owns infrastructure, not buildings. Income comes from tolls, annuities from authorities or tariffs, so it depends on contracts, traffic and regulation. At least 90% of net distributable cash flows must be paid out, at least every six months. Assets have long lives but can lose value as concessions run down.
